surface_mechanism_description: The surface mechanism involves alternating Cd and Te reconstructions during the ALE cycle. Starting from a (231) Te-rich surface, exposure to Cd forms a c(2 32) 1(2 31) Cd-rich half-filled surface. Upon Te exposure, a (231) Te-rich surface is reformed with half-monolayer coverage. This cycle repeats, leading to a self-regulated growth rate of 0.5 monolayers per cycle.
evidence: Starting from a flat (231) Te-rich surface [step (1)], a c(2 32) 1(2 31) Cd-rich half-filled surface is formed upon exposure to the Cd flux [step (2)]. At this point, the roughness of the surface is still minimum. When completing the first CdTe ALE cycle with Te exposure, a (231) Te-rich surface is reformed [step (3)]; small islands of CdTe are present on the surface, with a half-monolayer surface coverage. The surface roughness is then maximum. When beginning the second CdTe ALE cycle, a c(2 32) 1(2 31) Cd-rich half-filled surface is formed [step (4)], still with a maximum roughness. Upon completion of the second CdTe ALE cycle, a flat (231) Te-rich surface, similar to the starting surface, is again reformed [step (5)]. A full CdTe monolayer has been grown.
